dda7475a04:
This is a 60-question comprehensive practice bank. It covers all 6 published scenarios, with 10 questions per scenario.

A live exam also has 60 items, but it draws from 4 of those 6 scenarios. The official guide doesn't specify a fixed number of items per scenario. So use this bank for broad coverage and pacing. It isn't a replica of a live form, or a predictor of your scaled score.

The practice distribution is D1 16, D3 12, D4 12, D2 11, D5 9, rounded from the official domain weights. Eight practice items are multiple-response and say Choose 2. Twelve items are adapted from the official guide's published sample questions (not verbatim). The other 48 are guide-authored practice items.
55bace1496: Answer every item in a scenario before opening its answers. Each answer note gives the correct option and why it's right. It explains why each distractor is wrong, and names the task statement it tests and the chapter that covers it. The answer key and a scoring guide are at the end.
19c64639b9:
The exam is written around production evidence: a log line, a metric, a symptom a team reports.

The strongest habit is to read each item in a fixed order. The order tells you which task statement is being tested, before the options pull you toward a familiar answer. Work the stem first, the evidence second, and the options last. Use the options to confirm a prediction, not to generate one.

This practice bank scores multi-select items by exact match. The official guide confirms that these items state how many responses to select. It doesn't specify the live exam's partial-credit or penalty rules, so check the current candidate instructions.

The bands below are study-planning heuristics only. A raw score here can't be converted to the official scaled score, or used to estimate pass probability.
835f319d7a: 48 or more overall and no domain in "study more": strong performance on this practice bank, but not proof of exam readiness. Review weak task statements, and explain every miss before relying on this result.
a9b82706e8: 41 or fewer, or any domain in "study more": revisit the listed chapters and their mini-labs, then retake in a week. Recall will inflate your second score. So judge by whether you can explain each distractor, not by the number.
f21c4cbffb: Timing: 120 minutes for 60 items is 2 minutes each. If you needed more than 100 minutes, practise this order: read the scenario context once, then read the stem for the production evidence (logs, metrics), and only then the options.
a421fe6205:
A score tells you how you did. The pattern of misses tells you what to do.

For each wrong answer, write three things in a table: which distractor family you chose, which task statement the item tested, and whether you misread the evidence or lacked the concept.

  • Misreading is a method problem. Go back to the reading order.
  • A missing concept is a content problem. Re-read the chapter and run its companion example.

Two or more misses in the same family means you hold a wrong rule. The fix is to restate the rule in your own words, then find the test or example that proves it.
